A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BEAT framework. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched despite the revised title and appendix organization.

before.justification: v1 reports original embodied-agent experiments on VAB-OmniGibson and EB-ALFRED, including benchmark results, training-data-ratio analyses and out-of-distribution trigger tests.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds hyperparameter sensitivity, SFT ablation, prompt robustness, imperfect-trigger case studies and defense results.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same policy formulation, three dataset components, SFT stage and CTL objective with preference and NLL terms. The new CTL-only experiment is an ablation, not a revision of BEAT; replacing MLLM terminology with VLM does not change the method.

E1.justification: The household benchmarks, knife/vase tasks and original dataset coverage remain unchanged. Appendices C and E add evaluation with rewritten and safety-augmented system prompts, extending tested input conditions within the retained tasks.

E2.justification: The original Table 1 comparator set is retained. v2 adds BEAT w/o SFT at two backdoor-data ratios in Table 3 and evaluates activation clustering, a safety-prompt defense and continual benign SFT in Appendix E. Blur and smoothing are discussed without reported evaluations.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce alpha/beta sweeps, CTL-only controls at k=0.5 and 1.0, prompt alterations and defense-specific testing. The original test pools, model sizes and training schedules remain unchanged. FTR's inclusion in Section 4.1 and Table 1 expands its presentation; v1 already used this metric in Section 4.3.

E4.justification: v2 substantially broadens the diagnostic evidence beyond the retained data-ratio, false-triggering, OOD and error analyses. It adds tests of hyperparameter sensitivity and SFT necessity (Tables 2–3), prompt robustness (Appendix C), partial/multiple-vase case studies (Appendix D/Figure 7), and attack detection or removal through defenses (Appendix E).

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests for these experiments. The added results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Original Table 1 SR, ASR and F1 values are retained, but v2 substantially expands reported findings: CTL-only ASRs of 58.1%/67.6%, rewritten-prompt ASR of 65.9%, safety-prompt ASR of 64.7%, and 0% ASR after continual benign SFT. New FTR entries also introduce unresolved conflicts: EB-ALFRED Qwen2-VL without CTL is 22.5% in Table 1 versus 17% in the retained Figure 5, while InternVL3 BEAT is 0% versus 4%. These conflicts do not establish reliable performance changes.

T1.justification: The formal policy-switching definition, dataset equations and training objectives remain unchanged. v2 adds empirical analyses and discussion, without new mathematical assumptions, propositions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions and claims: object-based visual backdoors, SFT followed by CTL, approximately 80% attack success, up to 39% activation-F1 improvement and OOD generalization. The added experiments support these retained headline claims.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation and applicability boundaries. It explains the complementary roles of SFT and CTL, motivates simple object triggers relative to more complex alternatives, discusses defense effectiveness and resource tradeoffs, and explicitly acknowledges simulation-only validation. The original API and bounding-box limitations are retained in Appendix F.

D1.justification: v2 documents the prompt-rewriting instruction, exact safety instruction, and activation-clustering procedure using final-token last-layer features, PCA and two-cluster KMeans. Original implementation settings and prompt templates are retained. The promise to release code upon acceptance is removed; neither that deletion nor the retained project link establishes actual code availability.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and main related-work discussion remain unchanged. New Section 5 explicitly positions CTL as the first preference-learning-style training for inserting precisely activated backdoors, and Appendix E relates its benign-SFT defense findings to the already cited Ni et al. (2024).

P1.justification: v2 revises the title, standardizes MLLM terminology to VLM, corrects grammar and adds an object-trigger discussion section. It reorganizes the appendices, moving prompts from C to H, limitations from D to F, and the existing ethics statement to G. Most original exposition remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds sensitivity and SFT-ablation Tables 2–3 and imperfect-trigger Figure 7, expands Table 1 with FTR columns, and revises Figure 1 labels. Existing appendix tables are retained as Tables 4–6, with corresponding layout and numbering adjustments; the original analytical plots remain.

improvement.justification: The new SFT ablation strengthens the rationale for two-stage training, while prompt and defense tests make attack robustness and vulnerability to benign fine-tuning more assessable. Expanded limitations also clarify the simulation-only evidence. These gains are constrained by incompletely specified defense experiments and new Table 1/Figure 5 FTR inconsistencies, yielding a limited overall improvement.
